shared_source_contexts.context_summary: A 4.0 M aqueous sodium chloride solution, 500 mL aliquot, is electrolysed; atomic masses for Na and Hg and the Faraday constant are supplied.

questions.stem_summary: Classify the reaction in which white phosphorus reacts with sodium hydroxide and phosphine is one product.

difficulty.basis: A direct redox-pattern classification once oxidation states in the products are recognized.

answer_verification.independent_check: Phosphorus starts at oxidation state 0; in the products it is reduced to -3 in PH3 and oxidized to +1 in hypophosphite, so the same element undergoes both directions: disproportionation.

questions.common_wrong_route: Classify by product appearance or reaction setting instead of tracking phosphorus oxidation states.
reasoning_route: Assign phosphorus oxidation state in elemental P.
Identify one reduced and one oxidized phosphorus product.
Classify simultaneous oxidation and reduction of the same element as disproportionation.
questions.stable_crux_move: Track the same element into two products with oxidation states on opposite sides of its starting value.

questions.stem_summary: Five moles of hydrogen sulfide react completely with acidified permanganate; determine the requested sum involving water formed and electrons transferred.

source_answer.authority: official answer-key URL not located in archive during pass

difficulty.basis: Requires correct acidic-medium half-reaction accounting, electron count and stoichiometric scaling to the supplied amount.

answer_verification.independent_check: Balanced ionic equation: 2 MnO4^- + 5 H2S + 6 H+ -> 2 Mn2+ + 5 S + 8 H2O. For 5 mol H2S, water x=8 mol and electrons y=10 mol, so x+y=18.

questions.common_wrong_route: Count water or permanganate coefficients before balancing both charge and atoms in acidic medium, or count only 5 electrons instead of 10.
reasoning_route: Write oxidation of sulfide sulfur from -2 to 0 and reduction of Mn(+7) to Mn(+2).
Equalize the electron count and balance H/O in acidic medium.
Scale to 5 mol H2S and read water and total electrons transferred.
questions.stable_crux_move: Electron balance fixes the stoichiometric scale before water is counted.

questions.topic: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry / Mole Concept / Stoichiometry
questions.stem_summary: Using the shared NaCl electrolysis setup, determine the total amount of chlorine gas evolved.

difficulty.basis: Convert molarity and volume to chloride amount, then apply the 2 Cl- to 1 Cl2 stoichiometric ratio.

answer_verification.independent_check: 4.0 mol/L x 0.500 L gives 2.0 mol chloride. Since 2 Cl- produce 1 Cl2, the amount of chlorine is 1.0 mol, matching option B.

questions.common_wrong_route: Treat 2 mol of chloride ions as 2 mol of chlorine molecules.
reasoning_route: Convert 4.0 M and 0.500 L to moles of NaCl/Cl-.
Apply the electrode stoichiometry 2 Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e-.
questions.stable_crux_move: Use molecular chlorine's two-chloride stoichiometry after converting concentration to amount.

questions.topic: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry / Mole Concept / Stoichiometry
questions.stem_summary: With mercury as the cathode in the shared electrolysis setup, determine the maximum mass of amalgam formed.

difficulty.basis: Requires carrying the shared 2 mol sodium inventory into the stated amalgam mass calculation and using the supplied atomic masses.

answer_verification.independent_check: The 500 mL of 4.0 M NaCl contains 2 mol Na+. Complete cathodic uptake gives 2 mol Na in Na-Hg amalgam; with the paper's implied 1:1 NaHg composition and supplied masses, 2(23+200)=446 g, matching option D.

questions.common_wrong_route: Report only the deposited sodium mass, or omit the mercury contribution to the amalgam mass.
reasoning_route: Carry forward the 2 mol Na+ inventory from the shared stem.
Use the cathode/amalgam stoichiometric composition implied by the source item.
Convert the resulting formula amount to mass with the supplied atomic masses.
questions.stable_crux_move: The requested mass is the amalgam mass, not the sodium deposit alone.

questions.topic: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry / Mole Concept / Stoichiometry
questions.stem_summary: Using the shared NaCl electrolysis setup and the supplied Faraday constant, determine the total charge required for complete electrolysis.

difficulty.basis: Convert solution amount to electron amount and then use the Faraday charge-per-mole conversion.

answer_verification.independent_check: The solution contains 2 mol NaCl, so complete electrolysis transfers 2 mol electrons. Charge=2 x 96500 C=193000 C, matching option D.

questions.common_wrong_route: Use one Faraday for the full 2 mol NaCl inventory.
reasoning_route: Convert solution concentration and volume to 2 mol NaCl.
Associate one electron per Na+ discharged, hence 2 mol electrons.
Multiply by the supplied Faraday constant.
questions.stable_crux_move: Convert the reacting amount into moles of electrons before converting electrons into charge.
